topic.title: Experiment tracking — MLflow, W&B and reproducibility

outcomes: Design reproducible experiment runs with immutable parameters, versioned datasets, metrics and artifacts.
Compare MLflow Tracking and Weights & Biases run/project/artifact concepts and trade-offs.
Build dataset manifests with content hashes, split lineage and leakage checks.
Track metrics as step-indexed time series and compare runs using declared objectives.
Reproduce training using code commit, environment lock, seeds, hardware and dataset snapshot.
Protect experiment metadata and artifacts from secret/PII leakage.
prerequisites: Stage 1 Python/data foundations and Stage 2–4 ML/DL training fundamentals
Git, virtual environments, dataset splitting, metrics and basic model training

glossary.definition: A named collection of related training runs addressing one research question.
One execution with parameters, metrics, code/environment metadata and artifacts.
A run configuration value normally immutable once logged.
A measured value recorded at a step/time, often as a time series.
A file or directory produced or consumed by a run, such as model, plot, checkpoint or dataset manifest.
A versioned description of files, hashes, schema, splits and provenance.
The trace linking dataset, code, configuration, model and downstream evaluation.
The ability to rerun or explain an experiment using its recorded inputs and environment.
A coordinated search over hyperparameter configurations.
A governed catalog of model versions and promotion stages, separate from experiment tracking.

explanation.problem: Machine learning progress is easy to lose. A notebook may show accuracy 94%, but without the exact dataset version, split, code commit, preprocessing, seed, hyperparameters, environment and checkpoint, the result cannot be trusted or reproduced. Experiment tracking turns informal trial-and-error into an auditable scientific workflow.
explanation.plainLanguage:
An experiment groups runs around one question, such as whether a deeper model improves validation accuracy. A run records configuration parameters, metric time series, tags, dataset references, source-code commit, environment and output artifacts. Keep the experiment name stable and give each run a unique ID. Do not overwrite a previous run when a configuration changes.

Parameters describe what you set before training: learning rate, batch size, optimizer, model depth, seed, data split and augmentation. Treat parameters as immutable once recorded. Metrics describe what happened: training loss, validation loss, accuracy, F1, latency or memory. Metrics often have a step and timestamp; keep the full history rather than only the final summary. State the direction of optimization and evaluation split.

MLflow Tracking organizes experiments and runs, with parameters, metrics, tags and artifacts stored by a tracking backend. Its tracking server can use a database for metadata and an artifact store for files. MLflow model logging and registry features build on tracking, but a run is not automatically a promoted production model. Choose backend storage, authentication, artifact access and retention deliberately.

Weights & Biases organizes work into projects and runs, with config, step-based history, summaries, tags, artifacts and lineage. Artifacts can version datasets, checkpoints and model outputs. Sweeps coordinate hyperparameter search strategies. Teams should understand project privacy, artifact access, offline logging/sync, entity ownership and retention before uploading proprietary data.

Dataset identity is more than a filename. Build a manifest with immutable dataset version, file paths, content hashes, schema, row count, source, license, preprocessing code version and split membership. Keep train/validation/test IDs disjoint. Never tune against the test set; reserve it for final unbiased evaluation. If data changes, create a new dataset version rather than silently mutating an existing one.

Reproducibility metadata includes Git commit and dirty state, dependency lockfile hash, Python/library versions, OS/container image, hardware/accelerator, random seeds, deterministic settings, training config, dataset snapshot, preprocessing pipeline and model initialization. Seeds help but do not guarantee bitwise determinism across hardware, kernels or distributed training. Record limitations instead of promising perfect reproducibility.

Compare runs using the same evaluation dataset and metric definition. A higher accuracy on a different split is not a valid win. Use tables/plots for metric trajectories and declare the primary objective before looking at results. Track resource use and cost alongside quality; a 0.2% gain may not justify 4× training cost.

Sweeps can explore grid, random or Bayesian configurations. Start with a bounded search space and fixed validation protocol. Avoid using test metrics to choose hyperparameters. Use early stopping or pruning only when it does not bias comparisons. Preserve exact configuration and sweep agent version for every run.

Artifacts should be content-addressed and linked to the run: checkpoints, model weights, confusion matrices, plots, evaluation reports and dataset manifests. Store large artifacts in object storage, not as database blobs. Record artifact URI, SHA-256, size, media type and access policy. Verify hashes on download and promotion.

Tracking systems can leak sensitive information. Never log passwords, access tokens, connection strings, raw PII, unredacted prompts or sensitive training samples. Use metadata allowlists, artifact ACLs, encryption, retention/deletion policies and audit logs. Redact exception messages and command lines that may contain secrets.

Experiment tracking is not evaluation governance or a model registry. Tracking explains how a candidate was trained; evaluation establishes whether it meets quality/safety thresholds; a registry governs version, approval and promotion. Connect these systems with immutable run IDs and artifact hashes rather than treating a logged checkpoint as production-ready.
explanation.mentalModel: Question → experiment → immutable run config + dataset snapshot → training → step-indexed metrics + artifacts → compare on same evaluation protocol → reproduce/promote separately.
limitations: A random seed does not guarantee bitwise determinism across GPU kernels, devices or distributed execution.
Metrics are comparable only when dataset split, preprocessing and metric definitions match.
Tracking metadata does not replace data governance, evaluation gates or model registry approvals.
Artifact hashes prove file integrity, not that the artifact is safe or scientifically valid.
Cloud tracking may transmit sensitive metadata or artifacts; configure privacy, ACLs and retention.
A notebook's final cell output is not a reproducible experiment record.
explanation.everydayAnalogy: A scientist keeps a lab notebook: exact ingredients, instrument settings, sample batch, procedure, observations and resulting samples. If another scientist cannot identify the sample or reproduce the procedure, the reported result is not reliable.
explanation.mathMadeSimple: Run A reaches validation accuracy 0.91 at epoch 8; Run B reaches 0.93 at epoch 12. If B used a different validation split, comparison is invalid. If both use the same dataset snapshot and metric, B gains 2 percentage points but takes 50% more epochs. Record quality and compute cost before choosing.
explanation.productionImpact: Production experiment tracking requires immutable run IDs, dataset manifests, source/environment hashes, step-indexed metrics, artifact checksums, access controls, secret redaction, retention, run comparison and integration with evaluation and registry gates.

useCase.scenario: A team compares logistic regression, a small neural network and a transformer baseline on the same versioned text dataset. Every run records split hashes, preprocessing commit, hyperparameters, seed, validation metrics, training duration and model artifacts.
constraints: Dataset snapshot and splits are immutable.
Parameters are recorded before training and cannot be silently changed.
All runs use the same validation protocol.
Secrets and raw PII are not logged.
Test set is reserved for final evaluation.
useCase.successMetric: A reviewer can reproduce the run configuration, verify dataset/artifact hashes and compare candidates on the same evaluation protocol.

dataFlow.payload: run ID + artifact hash + gate result

trustBoundaries: Tracking client receives scoped credentials; secrets are never stored in run params or tags.
Dataset and artifact stores enforce tenant/project ACLs.
Artifact downloads verify content hash and scan untrusted files.
Metric and metadata logging uses allowlists to prevent PII/secret leakage.
Promotion to registry requires independent evaluation and approval.
failurePaths: Mutable dataset overwritten: reject and create a new content-hashed dataset version.
Run parameter changed after start: fail immutable-parameter check.
Metric logged with wrong split: tag evaluation split and block invalid comparison.
Artifact upload interrupted: resume/checksum and mark incomplete until verified.
Tracking backend unavailable: bounded local/offline buffer with explicit sync status.
Secret/PII detected in metadata: redact/block upload and emit security event.
Different code/environment: mark run non-reproducible rather than claiming exact replay.

Log code commit, dependency lock, seed, optimizer, learning rate and batch size before training.

Both use same validation protocol; B improves accuracy by 0.02 but uses 50% more epochs.
Check checkpoint SHA-256 and source/environment/dataset hashes before evaluation handoff.

workedExample.expectedOutput: Run B is a valid validation improvement candidate, but it still needs independent test-set evaluation and registry approval.

failures.name: Dataset drift hidden
failures.symptom: A rerun reports different metrics under same dataset name.
failures.rootCause: Dataset file or split mutated without new version.
failures.recovery: Content-hashed manifest and immutable split membership.
failures.regressionTest: Modify one source file and assert dataset hash changes.

failures.name: Parameter overwrite
failures.symptom: Run appears to have one config but actually trained with another.
failures.recovery: Make run params immutable; create a new run for changes.
failures.regressionTest: Second log_param with different value is rejected.

failures.name: Invalid run comparison
failures.symptom: Candidate B appears better because it used an easier validation split.
failures.recovery: Compare only runs with same dataset snapshot and metric definition.

failures.name: Artifact corruption
failures.symptom: Downloaded checkpoint differs from uploaded file.
failures.rootCause: No checksum or incomplete artifact upload.
failures.recovery: Record SHA-256 and verify on retrieval.
failures.regressionTest: Corrupted artifact bytes fail checksum verification.

failures.name: Secret leakage
failures.symptom: API token or PII appears in run tags or artifacts.
failures.recovery: Allowlist fields, redact secrets and enforce artifact ACLs.

failures.name: False reproducibility claim
failures.symptom: Run cannot be recreated despite same seed.
failures.recovery: Record commit, lockfile, hardware and deterministic limitations.
failures.regressionTest: Reproduction report identifies missing metadata as incomplete.

scenarioQuiz.question: What should change when a dataset file changes?
options: Create a new immutable dataset version and hash
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Dataset identity is content-based; changed data creates a new version and lineage.

scenarioQuiz.question: Can a run's logged parameter be overwritten after training starts?
options: No, create a new run for changed configuration
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Run parameters should be immutable to preserve experiment provenance.

scenarioQuiz.question: Which metadata best supports reproducibility?
options: Code commit, lockfile, dataset/splits, config, hardware and artifacts
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Reproduction requires the full input and execution context, not only a seed.

scenarioQuiz.question: Run B scores higher but uses a different validation split. What is correct?
options: Compare only after aligning dataset and metric protocol
Use test set to tune both
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Metrics are comparable only when evaluation datasets and definitions match.

rubric.evidence: Runs have immutable params, unique IDs and clear objective.
Manifest hashes, schema and disjoint split IDs are recorded.
Step-indexed metrics and verified artifacts are persisted.
Code/environment/seed are recorded and only compatible runs are compared.
Secrets/PII are redacted and artifact access is controlled.

evidence: Metric history and artifact hash persist across restart.

codeWalkthrough.explanation: A dataset name is not identity; content and split hashes are.
Parameters are immutable run configuration; changed values require a new run.
Step-indexed metric history supports curves, early stopping and reproducible comparisons.
Artifact hashes detect corruption and preserve provenance.
